# A claim on a good first issue waits hours for any reply

## Context

A claim on a curated issue waits until a maintainer seat happens to run:

- `#19143`, 2026-09-23 15:40Z: a first-time contributor claimed it. The first reply, the assignment, came 27.5 h later and said "your comment reached nobody for a day".
- `#19143` again, 2026-09-25 07:59Z: a second first-timer claimed it, 13 h after the assignment. The reply came 2 h later, after the assignee's PR had opened.
- `#19140`, 2026-09-24 18:20Z: a claim, then a withdrawal 16 minutes later ("I can't self-assign it"), with no reply in between.

Hacktoberfest opens on 2026-10-01 (#18985). In October 2025, 20 people opened 60 external PRs.

## The Problem

- The claim rule is CONTRIBUTING §3 item 3 (#19195): the first claimant is assigned, the first approve-worthy PR wins, and assignment protects your time. It only protects the claimant if they hear back in time.
- A seat runs when the operator starts one. Heartbeats are off on purpose (daytime noise), and @tobiu ruled on 2026-09-24 that a 20–30 min heartbeat would be too slow anyway. neo-agent-brain#468 took the heartbeat path and was closed on that ruling.
- @tobiu's rule from 2025 for a late claimant is to offer a different ticket, because someone else has started.
- **Maintainers are not online around the clock** (@tobiu, 2026-09-25). The operator sleeps about 8 h, and rate limits keep AI seats from running 24/7. So every step that needs a maintainer, confirming an assignment included, waits for the next session, and that can be many hours away. A workflow is the one participant that is always there, and on a public repository it costs no seat time.

## The Architectural Reality

- No workflow in `.github/workflows/` triggers on `issue_comment` today.
- Siblings: `prevent-reopen.yml` answers an issue event with inline `actions/github-script@v9`. CI logic that carries a spec lives in `buildScripts/util/check-*.mjs`, with specs in `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/`.
- An `issue_comment` run uses the workflow file from the default branch (`dev`), holds a write token, and reads untrusted text.
- Curated means `good first issue` or `help wanted`. Only `neomjs/neo` has open good first issues (6 on 2026-09-25).

## The Fix

`.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`, on `issue_comment` `[created]`, for issues (not PRs) that carry either label. It replies at most once per (issue, user), and only to a comment with claim intent:

| State when the claim arrives | The reply |
|---|---|
| free: no assignee, no open linked PR, no earlier claim | "you're first in line and can start now; a maintainer confirms the assignment when one is online, which can take a while" |
| an earlier claimant, still unassigned | who asked first, plus alternatives |
| assigned | the assignee, plus alternatives |
| an open PR resolves it | the PR, plus alternatives |

**Through a maintainer gap, the first-in-line reply is the claimant's protection.** Later claimants are pointed elsewhere, so the first one starts at once instead of waiting hours for an assignment. The assignment confirms it afterwards.

Alternatives come from the live `no:assignee -linked:pr` set for the same label, excluding this issue. They must not give everyone the same short list; that funnel is what produced `#19143`.

The workflow never assigns. Assignment stays with a seat, which is what screens out spray accounts. An account that sprays claim templates across repositories gets skipped, and the next human is confirmed. The known cost: during a gap, a spray account that claims first holds the ticket until a seat screens it. That hold ends at the next session, and the workflow offers everyone else alternatives in the meantime.

Requirements from @neo-opus-ada, the #18985 steward, 2026-09-24:

1. **Claim intent, once.** Patterns such as "work on", "claim", "assign", "take this", `/assign`, matched on the comment without its quoted lines. No reply to questions, thanks, maintainers, bots or the assignee.
2. **Injection-safe.** `actions/github-script`, reading the body from `context.payload`, never `${{ github.event.comment.body }}` in a `run:` step. Check out only the default branch. `permissions: issues: write`, plus `pull-requests: read` only if the linked-PR read measurably needs it.
3. **No promise the workflow can't keep.** "A maintainer confirms" names no time, and the reply says a confirmation can take a while, so the claimant starts instead of waiting.

The intent classifier and the reply choice go into one pure module beside the `check-*.mjs` siblings, with a spec. The fixtures come from real threads: the three claims above, plus non-claims that must not trigger. The most important non-claim is the assignee's thank-you on `#19143`, which contains "work on the fix" and quotes "it's yours".

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a workflow comment on a curated issue | CONTRIBUTING §3 item 3 (#19195) | the table above | no reply; a seat answers, as today | one clause in CONTRIBUTING §3 item 3: a claim gets an automatic reply that says where you stand, and first in line may start before a maintainer confirms (wording agreed with @neo-opus-ada, whose sentence it extends) | the spec, plus the first reply after merge |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A claim by a non-member on a curated issue gets one reply, matching the table, within a minute.
- [ ] The first-in-line reply says the claimant can start now and that the confirmation can take a while, and it names no time.
- [ ] Questions, thanks, quoted text, the assignee's own comments, and maintainer and bot comments get no reply. The spec covers each case, using the fixtures above.
- [ ] At most one reply per (issue, user), across edits and re-runs.
- [ ] The workflow never assigns, never interpolates the comment into a shell step, and checks out only `dev`. Its permissions are only what it needs, and the PR says why each one is there.
- [ ] Alternatives come from the live query, exclude the current issue, and don't send every redirect to the same ticket.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING §3 item 3 has the clause from the ledger.
- [ ] Post-merge, flagged: the first real claim after merge gets its reply, linked here.

## Out of Scope

- Assigning.
- The PR-side case, a non-assignee's PR against an assigned issue (the operator's "day 5" gap). It gets a leaf of its own if it recurs.
- Other repositories. When a second repository curates good first issues, lift the module into `neo-agent-skills`' reusable workflows.

## Avoided Traps

- **A `/claim` auto-assign bot.** It hands first-timer issues to whoever sprays claims fastest.
- **The heartbeat path** (neo-agent-brain#468). Heartbeats are disabled on purpose, and too slow even when they run.
- **Replying to every comment.** A reply to a question or a spam comment amplifies the noise that turning heartbeats off removed.
- **A spray screen inside the workflow** (account age, fork count). A real first-timer's account is often new too, so the screen stays with a seat.
- **"We'll assign you soon."** No seat is always online, so the only honest time is none.
